title: Carrier duality from the convergence of Dirac fermions and high-order van Hove singularities
authors: Meng Lyu, Kaiyi Zhai, Nikolai Peshcherenko, Junyan Liu, Jinying Yang, Subir Sen, Binbin Wang, Langsheng Ling, Zhaosheng Wang, Gang Li, Jieyi Liu, Yang Xu, Xiyang Li, Claudia Felser, Yang Zhang, Wujun Shi, Lexian Yang, Enke Liu
abstract: The convergence of highly mobile Dirac fermions and flat-band heavy electrons offers a paradigm for emergent quantum phenomena. However, experimental realization of such intriguing state remains elusive. In this study, we report a dual carrier regime in the kagome metal Co3In2S2, wherein the charge transport is governed by high-mobility electrons while the thermodynamic responses exhibit heavy-electron behavior. This exotic duality arises from the coexistence of topological Dirac fermions and flat-band high-order (4th-order) Van Hove singularities (HOVHSs) at the Fermi surface, as revealed by magnetic-torque quantum oscillation and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. The interaction between Dirac and HOVHS-derived carriers can be captured by a minimal two-pocket model, manifesting as sublinear resistivity above ~100 K and field-induced non-Fermi-liquid behavior at low temperatures. Our study establishes Co3In2S2 as a model platform for exploring many-body physics at the intersection of topology and correlation effects, and provides a foundational framework for designing quantum materials hosting diverse emergent states.
summary: This work reports on the kagome metal Co3In2S2, demonstrating a unique carrier duality where its transport properties suggest high mobility while its thermodynamics point to heavy electron behavior. This exotic state arises from the simultaneous presence of topological Dirac fermions and flat bands originating from high-order Van Hove singularities at the Fermi level. The study uses ARPES and quantum oscillations to confirm this coexistence, establishing the material as a model platform for correlated physics.
main_problem: The study investigates emergent quantum phenomena arising from the coexistence and interaction between highly mobile Dirac fermions and flat-band heavy electrons in a specific material.
main_result: The kagome metal Co3In2S2 exhibits a carrier duality where charge transport is governed by high-mobility electrons, while thermodynamic responses show heavy-electron behavior due to the interplay between Dirac fermions and high-order Van Hove singularities (HOVHSs).
method: The research combines advanced experimental techniques, including Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) and quantum oscillation measurements, with theoretical modeling using a minimal two-pocket model.
model_or_system: The physical system is the kagome metal Co3In2S2. The theoretical framework involves modeling the electronic structure using a minimal two-pocket model that captures the hybridization between topological Dirac cones and flat bands derived from 4th-order Van Hove singularities (HOVHSs) at the Fermi surface.
key_observables: Carrier duality (high mobility transport vs. heavy electron thermodynamics), sublinear resistivity ($ho_{xx} \propto T^{0.53}$), Non-Fermi-liquid (NFL) behavior ($ho_{xx} \propto T^{1.5}$), large Sommerfeld coefficient ($\gamma$), and distinct band dispersions visible via ARPES.
important_parameters: Temperature regimes (high T vs. low T), magnetic field strength (up to 35 T), and the exponents characterizing the resistivity scaling ($n \approx 1.5$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting the band dispersion near the HOVHS using a quartic function ($E \propto k^4$) and modeling the transport using a two-band/two-pocket approach.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, the heavy-electron nature via $\gamma$ vs $T$, the sublinear/NFL temperature dependence of resistivity, and ARPES results confirming the coexisting Dirac and HOVHS features.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence for the exotic electronic state: first establishing the structural and electronic features (ARPES/DFT), then quantifying the heavy-fermion nature (thermodynamics/QO), and finally synthesizing these findings to explain the observed carrier duality and anomalous transport regimes.
why_interesting: The concept of carrier duality—where different physical responses (transport vs. thermodynamics) are governed by different electronic components—is a rich topic for understanding emergent quantum states in strongly correlated materials.
